/answer [auto-answered-by-orchestrator]

Auto-answered by the orchestrator clarify-respond workflow.

DECISIONS:
Q1: A
Q2: A

RATIONALE:
Q1: The bounded check this issue asks for already exists. Both `release` jobs already run `bash scripts/release_ci_gate.sh "${GATE_REPO}" "${RELEASE_TESTED_SHA}"` (`test-and-mark-stable.yml:6356`, `mark-stable.yml:696`), from #6797, which is closed. The weakness that remains is in the "Verify CI passed on source branch" steps of both `validate` jobs (`test-and-mark-stable.yml:6241-6283`, `mark-stable.yml:~600-634`). They still read the combined status from `commits/<sha>/status` and continue when it is empty or pending. Option A fixes exactly that by reusing the existing gate, instead of writing a second one as option C would.
Q2: The issue's default-off flag would stop every stable release (auto-release and the promote cycle) and add no protection, because the release jobs already fail closed on CI. A default-on kill switch keeps current releases running and still gives an operator a way to stop tag writes. Under §2 and §6 that is the lower-risk reading. It is reversible by changing one default.

EXECUTION PLAN (required for any non-letter decision):
Q1:
  strategy: derive_from_repo
  inputs:
    - .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml (validate step "Verify CI passed on source branch", lines ~6241-6283; release gate call at ~6356)
    - .github/workflows/mark-stable.yml (validate step at ~600-634; release gate call at ~696)
    - scripts/release_ci_gate.sh (existing bounded `ci.yml` / `lint` check-run gate, with `RELEASE_CI_GATE_WAIT_SECS` and `RELEASE_CI_GATE_POLL_SECS`)
  steps:
    - In both `validate` jobs, replace the `commits/${SHA}/status` lookup with a call to `scripts/release_ci_gate.sh "${{ github.repository }}" "$(git rev-parse HEAD)"`. Pass every `${{ }}` value through `env:` first.
    - The new check must require a successful newest `ci.yml` run for that exact SHA. It must fail closed when the run is missing, failed, cancelled, timed out, or unreadable. Keep the step `name:` unchanged.
    - When `inputs.gate_only` is true in `test-and-mark-stable.yml`, report a gate failure as `::warning::` and exit 0 instead of failing the step. `mark-stable.yml` has no `gate_only`, so there it always fails closed.
    - Grant `checks: read` and `actions: read` to the `validate` jobs if they don't already have them, so the gate works with `github.token`.
    - Add contract tests (e.g. extend the existing release-gate tests, or add `tests/test_release_validate_ci_gate.py`). They should check that neither `validate` job calls `commits/.*/status`, that both call `release_ci_gate.sh`, and that `gate_only` is warning-only.
    - Add a changelog fragment `changelog.d/7029-release-validate-ci-gate.md`.
  replaces_acceptance_criterion: "replace both status-based CI gates with a bounded check of the newest ci.yml run" becomes "replace the two remaining status-based checks (in the validate jobs), reusing the existing bounded gate".
  equivalence_argument: The release jobs already meet the criterion. After this change, no status-based gate is left in either workflow, so the intent of finding #6548 is fully met.
  reversibility: Small revert of two step bodies. The legacy status check is preserved in git history.
Q2:
  strategy: reframe
  inputs:
    - .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml (`release` job tag/release writes)
    - .github/workflows/mark-stable.yml (`release` job tag/release writes)
    - README.md variables table
  steps:
    - In both `release` jobs, add `RELEASE_TAGGING_ENABLED: ${{ vars.RELEASE_TAGGING_ENABLED || 'true' }}` to `env:`. Any shell that reads it must also default it to `true` (§8).
    - When the value is not `true` (case-insensitive), skip the tag push and release-creation steps with `::warning::RELEASE_TAGGING_ENABLED=false — skipping tag writes`. The CI gate and validation still run.
    - Add a README row: `RELEASE_TAGGING_ENABLED`, default `true`, a kill switch for stable tag writes in both release workflows.
    - Add a contract test that both release jobs carry the guard with the `true` default and that tag writes are conditioned on it.
  replaces_acceptance_criterion: "default-off RELEASE_TAGGING_ENABLED guard" becomes "default-on kill switch".
  equivalence_argument: The default-off flag was meant to keep unvalidated behaviour off. Tag writes are already protected by the fail-closed gate, and Q1 removes the last status-based check. Defaulting off would only pause releases and would make `auto-release-stable.yml` and the promote cycle fail silently, with no added security.
  reversibility: An operator can set the repo variable `RELEASE_TAGGING_ENABLED=false` to stop tagging right away. If a person wants the issue's literal default-off, they change the `'true'` fallback to `'false'` in two `env:` lines.
